# Code overrides: the remaining S2XX hand edits generated by CoGeNT

Date: 2026-10-12. Design approved in chat ("Approve (Recommended)").

## Goal

Generating the 40024 DBC with the user's settings reproduces the official S2XX workspace (read only:
`D:\networkgen\dc.app.scl.vehiclecomm`, repository layout copy `C:\Users\senth\Downloads\dc.app.scl.vehiclecomm`)
except for a short, documented list. Every hand edit that a plain generation could not reproduce becomes a
setting on a new GUI page "Code overrides" or an automatic generator fix. Output without overrides stays
byte-identical to today (golden tests), except the CRANK_COUNT compile fix (section 2).

## 1. Settings (`data\CanOverrideConfiguration.data`, saved in configuration archives)

```
{
 "tx": {"<MSG>": {"attribute": "Periodic" | "Event" | "Periodic+Event", "period": <ms>, "offset": <ms>,
                  "confirmation": true}},
 "rx": {"<MSG>": {"timeout": <ms>}},
 "nm_tx": [{"message": "<Tx MSG>", "label": "<comment name>", "buffer": "<C buffer>"}],
 "host_forward": {"prefix": "REM_MSG_", "function": "host_update_msg"},
 "numeric_order": ["REM_MSG_"]
}
```
Every key is optional; an empty or missing file means no override.

- `tx.attribute` replaces the frame attribute derived from the DBC (`IL_TX_ATTR_PERIODIC`, `IL_TX_ATTR_EVENT`,
  `IL_TX_ATTR_PERIODIC | IL_TX_ATTR_EVENT`); with `Event` the periodic pointer is NULL. `period` / `offset`
  replace the two values of the message's row in the periodic transmit table (other rows keep theirs).
- `tx.confirmation` adds `IL_TX_ATTR_TXC_NOTIFY`, `&Vnim_<MSG>_Conf`, `&Vnim_<MSG>_PreCopy` and their extern
  declarations, as a debounced signal does (no function bodies are generated: they are project code).
- `rx.timeout` acts as the DBC cycle time of the message (`GenMsgCycleTime`) in every generator: receive
  timeout count and the VNIM timeout cases (TC_NSM: 100).
- `nm_tx` replaces the single-entry `NM_TX_MSG_DATA_STRUCT` of nw_nm_par.h by one entry per row, in order:
  label comment, `CAN_GPNUM_8`, the message ID (upper-case hex), `&<buffer>[0]`, `CANB_TX_STD_DATA`,
  `(DLL_NUM_IL_TX_FRAMES+<n>)` with n = 1, 2, ...
- `host_forward`: the indication of every receive message whose name starts with the prefix calls
  `<function>(VNIM_<MSG>);` instead of the `#if vnim_notify_used ... os_notify ... #endif` lines, and a
  `R E M    M A C R O S` block (`#define VNIM_<MSG> <index>`, messages in order) follows the
  `IS_*_DLC_FAULT` defines of nw_vnim_app_signals_par.c.
- `numeric_order`: message names that start with one of the prefixes and end in digits sort by that number
  (REM_MSG_2 before REM_MSG_10) everywhere messages are ordered by name; nothing else changes order.

## 2. Automatic

- The legacy PreCopy writes stray `rValue |= ...` lines for some multi-byte signals (EMS46_500
  CRANK_COUNT_IBS) where `rValue` is not declared: they are written commented out (`// rValue |= ...`), as
  in the workspace. The golden comparison with legacy runs applies the same change to the legacy files.
- MANUAL_ACTIONS.md: an `additional_rx_messages` entry whose message is not enabled says that enabling its
  Rx lets CoGeNT generate it; the nw_can_dll.c dispatch of a merged block is reported as done when the
  workspace's nw_can_dll.c (folder of the Re-apply edits page) maps every member ID.

## 3. GUI

Page "Code overrides" (sidebar, between Receive FIFO and Re-apply edits): sections Tx messages, Rx timeouts,
NM transmit table, Host forwarding, Numeric order; rows added from a message list of the loaded DBC and
removed per row; Save writes the settings file; invalid entries (unknown message, non-number) are named.

## 4. Deliverables

`S2XX_40024_max_match.cfg` and `S2XX_41490_max_match.cfg`: the user's settings plus BMS19_100 / BMS20_100
enabled (cell temperatures 0x1F4, notification 200ms_Delay_g1), every override above, debounce on
REMOTE_HV_CONNECT_REQ_TGU. The 40024 one, generated, equals the workspace except: the IC2_100 Tx signal
order (older generator), the revision-note comment of can_rxrule.cfg, and the corrections of
`2026-10-11-multiplex-generation-design.md` section 9.
